source_refs.note: Chapter 9 summary (PDF 137-138), with its definitions arranged as a table; related terms share rows.

blocks.text: This chapter covered how to stay safe online, how attacks work and how to defend against them, how to collaborate and design fairly, how to start a digital business, and the ethical, legal and environmental responsibilities that come with computing. The table brings together its main terms.

blocks.caption: Chapter 9 key terms
rows: Cybersecurity
Protecting computers, networks, data and accounts from unauthorised access, misuse, damage or attack
Online safety
Using the Internet carefully to protect personal information, devices and digital identity
Strong password
A hard-to-guess password mixing upper- and lower-case letters, numbers and symbols
Privacy settings / privacy policy
Options that control who sees your information / a statement of how an app or website collects, uses, stores and shares data
Digital collaboration / digital etiquette
Working together online with shared tools / polite, respectful, responsible online behaviour
Cyber threat
Any danger to digital systems, data or users, such as phishing, malware, ransomware, hacking and identity theft
Phishing / malware / ransomware
Fake messages or sites that trick users into giving details / harmful software / malware that locks files and demands payment
Two-factor authentication / biometric verification
Two forms of verification, such as a password and a phone code / identity confirmed by fingerprint, face or voice
Firewall / antivirus software
Controls incoming and outgoing traffic by security rules / detects, blocks and removes harmful software
Cryptography / data protection
Converting information into a secure form only authorised users can read / keeping information safe from loss, misuse, theft or unauthorised access
Accessibility
Designing systems that people with different abilities, needs and backgrounds can use easily
Intellectual property / data privacy laws
Legally owned creations of the mind / laws on how personal data is collected, stored, used and shared
E-waste / sustainable computing
Discarded electronic devices / using, designing and disposing of technology to reduce environmental harm
Entrepreneurship / digital entrepreneurship
Creating innovative business ideas and opportunities / building businesses with the Internet, social media, e-commerce and digital tools

items: Safe habits and settings; threats and defences (2FA, firewalls, encryption).
Collaboration with equity and accessibility; digital entrepreneurship.
Ethics, law (GDPR, PECA) and the environment (e-waste, sustainable computing).
